summary: Three American broadcasters, Joe Pyne, Wally George and Morton Downey Jr., built confrontational right-wing talk radio and combat TV from the 1940s to the 1980s, trading on outrage, bigotry and staged fights.

evidence.note: Pyne born in Chester, Pennsylvania, December 1924
1949 Kenosha: Pyne puts a caller on air, start of call-in radio
lung cancer diagnosis and death in 1970
Wally George born 1931 in Oakland, California
last Metzger interview around 1992, used as main_span end
George stops taping new shows, dies of pneumonia in 2003
Hot Seat taped in Orange County; Pyne's peak years also in Los Angeles
segment on George hosting White Aryan Resistance leader Tom Metzger
Downey roundtable airing black-on-white crime talking points
column tracing Downey's model to Fox News and modern polarization

notes: Three-part series with equal weight on three hosts, so all three are primary even though the title names only Pyne. main_span runs from Pyne's 1949 call-in invention to George's early-1990s peak and decline. US-CA chosen because Pyne's national fame and George's whole career happened there; Downey's TV show taped in Secaucus, NJ. Packet spells it Pine; standard spelling Pyne used.
